title: wt sync --json
description: What a rebase onto trunk would do to every worktree of a repository, as `wt sync --json` prints it on stdout: one overview object, or with --all, --roots or --profile an array of them, one per repository. It fetches trunk and each worktree branch's own remote (unless --no-fetch) and writes nothing else. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

target.description: What is assessed against or rebased onto (since 1.8.0): trunk, or the ref --onto names.

ref.description: The ref as given to --onto, or origin/<trunk>.

trunk.description: The target is trunk: no --onto was given.

upstream.description: The commit --upstream names: only the commits above it are replayed. Null without it.

ownRemote.description: Since 1.3.0: a branch against its own remote, the remote-tracking ref a push of it would replace: what is recorded for the branch (branch.<name>.wtPushTo), else the branch's own name on the remote git pushes it to (refs/remotes/origin/<branch> unless <branch>@{push} has that name on another remote, or branch.<name>.pushRemote or remote.pushDefault names one). Since 1.5.0 never a branch of another name that is not recorded, whatever <branch>@{push} is. Never the upstream as such: a branch cut from trunk often tracks trunk and pushes to its own name. See docs/json.md.

ref.description: The remote-tracking ref, as remote/branch (origin/feat/x); null only when no ref could be named: for none, and for unknown unless it is a ref that could not be compared.

state.description: none: nothing to check: the ref is trunk's, or does not exist. gone: the branch names a ref the remote no longer has. unknown: where a push lands cannot be read from a tracking ref (a mirror remote, several push URLs, a push URL that is another repository than the fetch URL), or the branches or the remotes cannot be read at all, or the two tips cannot be compared; a run goes on unchecked. Since 1.5.0 also a branch a run would rebase and not push: noPushReason is then non-null. inSync: the same commit. ahead: only the branch has commits of its own. behind: only the remote has; a run fast-forwards the branch first. rebased: both have, and the remote's are old versions of the branch's (its tip is a tip the branch once had, or every commit only it has is matched patch for patch); a run goes on. diverged: both have, otherwise; a run refuses unless --allow-diverged.

commit.description: The remote commit compared with; null for none, gone and unknown.

ahead.description: Commits only the branch has; null for none, gone and unknown.

behind.description: Commits only the remote has; null for none, gone and unknown.

fetched.description: true: the remote side is from this command's fetch. false: as last fetched (--no-fetch, trunk's fetch or this branch's own failed, or a remote whose fetch refspec is not the standard one).

blocks.description: Why a run would refuse for it; non-null only when a run would. diverged with state diverged, for a branch a run would rebase: --allow-diverged goes on. operation, dirty, session with state behind: it cannot be fast-forwarded, because a git operation is in progress there, the checkout has tracked changes, or an agent session is busy in it.

noPushReason.description: Since 1.5.0: why a run would rebase the branch and not push it, in words; null when a run would push it, and for state none. It tracks a remote branch of another name and nothing is recorded for it (state unknown, fixCommand settles it); what is recorded for it cannot be used (state unknown); or it is recorded as pushing to a branch of another name that has commits it never had, is at a commit it was never at, or cannot be compared with it (state diverged, behind, rebased or unknown). See docs/json.md.

fixCommand.description: Since 1.5.0: the command that settles noPushReason, as an argv, when one does: wt sync push-to <branch> <remote>/<branch>, which records the branch it tracks as where it pushes. The same command with the branch's own name on the remote records that instead. It names no directory: run it in the repository. Null otherwise.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

repo.description: The main checkout, as wt sweep --json names the repository.

name.description: The repository's name: its main checkout's directory name.

trunkSource.description: How trunk was determined, first match wins, from local refs alone (since 1.1.0): config — MAIN_BRANCH in the wt configuration file; originHead — refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; conventional — the first of development, main, master that exists locally or on origin (since 1.1.1; before, main, master, trunk, development, develop, ranked by where each exists); currentBranchGuess — no longer produced since 1.1.1: when nothing names trunk, detection fails and the repository reports noConfiguration. Null when trunk is.

trunkRef.description: origin/<trunk>, what every worktree is assessed against.

onto.description: The commit assessed against, or rebased onto: trunk, or --onto's target (since 1.8.0). Null when it was never determined.

target.description: What onto is: trunk, or the ref --onto names (since 1.8.0). Null when it was never determined.

fetchError.description: The fetch failed: the overview is against trunk as last fetched.

declared.description: Trunk declares .wt-sync.yaml. Without it the worktrees are assessed but a run rebases none.

token.description: Names what a run would start on; pass it to wt sync rebase --expect or wt sync --rebase --expect. Since 1.3.0 a worktree refused only for having diverged from its own remote is in it too, with the remote commit, for a run under --allow-diverged. Null when a run would start on nothing.

error.description: Why there is no overview: trunk not known, the repository not readable.

sessionsError.description: Agent sessions could not be listed; sessions are then empty, not known empty.

eachCommitDeclared.description: Since 1.6.0. The each_commit checks .wt-sync.yaml declares on the trunk commit in onto, in the declared order: each runs after every replayed commit that changes a path its paths match, every commit when it lists none. Empty when trunk declares none.

needs.description: Since 1.6.0. Every need a declared step has, once each, with what its probe said. A need is probed only when a step with it would run for some worktree of the overview: an each_commit step with a commit to check, or a deferred step whose paths match a path the rebase may change. A run probes the same way before it moves anything, and refuses a worktree whose step needs one that did not answer, unless started with --allow-owed.

probed.description: The probe ran: some worktree has a step with this need that would run.

ok.description: The probe answered. False when it did not, or was not run.

error.description: Why the probe failed; null when it answered or was not run.

worktrees.description: Every worktree but the main checkout, in git's order.

stack.description: Since 1.7.0: the stack held on the line of the worktree wt sync <work> --stack names: its layers and what holds each. Null without --stack.

group.description: The overview's group. current is on trunk already, which the human overview leaves out. Since 1.3.0 a worktree whose class is current or stale only at its remote's commit, which a run fast-forwards it to, is ready.

class.description: What the simulated rebase found; unknown when the assessment failed (error).

verified.description: false is the overview's question mark (recipe?): a script owns a path and the replay could not be carried past it.

verdict.description: What wt sync rebase <work> would do: start on it, skip it, or refuse it untouched.

runnable.description: wt sync --rebase, with nothing named, takes it.

reason.description: Why it is not runnable; null when it is.

handedOver.description: An earlier run left a conflict here for a person: wt sync resume or wt sync undo.

planFile.description: The plan file of a handover.

kind.description: Since 1.2.0 also codex: a Codex session.

stack.description: Every worktree a run on this one would move, parents first; just this one without a stack; empty when detached.

stops.description: Every stop the simulated rebase reached, in order.

strategies.description: The declared strategies that resolved a file at some stop, each once.

deferredDeclared.description: Since 1.4.0. The deferred steps .wt-sync.yaml declares on the trunk commit in onto, in the declared order: what a run goes through once it has rebased this worktree, itself or through wt sync resume after a handover. Declared, not predicted: each may run. A step with no paths does, after every finished rebase; one with paths only when the rebase changed one of them; none after a step that failed. The same list on every worktree, also one a run would skip or refuse, where nothing is rebased and so none runs: verdict says which. Empty when trunk declares none or has no .wt-sync.yaml.

checks.description: Since 1.6.0. How many of the branch's commits a run would check with the each_commit steps: those changing a path a step's paths match. Nothing is run to say so. A commit a resolution leaves with no matching change is not checked by the run, so this is an upper bound.

checkCommits.description: Since 1.6.0. The commits checks counts, oldest first, as they are on the branch now.

ownRemote.description: Since 1.3.0. A worktree a run would refuse for it has verdict refuse, runnable false and the reason in words; its group is needsYou, or skipped when a busy session is in it, whatever blocks says; class stays about trunk. For a branch that is behind and will be fast-forwarded, class, behind, ahead and stops are those of the remote commit: what the run rebases. When that class is current or stale there is nothing to rebase: the row is verdict proceed, runnable true, group ready, and a run fast-forwards the branch and is done.

declaredStep.description: One step .wt-sync.yaml on trunk declares under defer: or each_commit:, before any rebase. See docs/json.md.

step.description: Its run line: the string deferred[].step carries for it in wt sync rebase --json.

paths.description: The globs that gate it, as declared. For a deferred step: empty, it runs after every finished rebase; otherwise only when the rebase changed a path one of them matches, which is not known before the rebase. For an each_commit step: empty, it runs at every replayed commit; otherwise at each one changing a path one of them matches.

needs.description: Since 1.6.0. What the step cannot run without, as declared; the overview's needs says what each probe answered.

resolved.description: Every conflicted file here was resolved by a strategy.

yours.description: The first stop no strategy resolves: a run hands it to a person.

strategy.description: The strategy that claims it; null when none does.

note.description: Why a strategy refused it, or what a lift did.

stack.description: Since 1.7.0: a stack held on one line, for --stack: the line from where it leaves trunk (base) to its tip (head), and its layer branches, bottom first. See docs/json.md.

branch.description: The line's own branch: the worktree named.

base.description: Where the line leaves trunk: the merge base.

head.description: The line's tip before the run.

autosquash.description: A fold of the line's fixups onto its own base (--autosquash), not a rebase onto trunk.

refusal.description: The run's: why no layer moved: a new tip failed its check, or the fold changed the line's content. Null in the look, and when each layer was moved or held.

stackLayer.description: Since 1.7.0: one layer of a stack held on one line. The look fills what it sees; a run also fills what came of the layer, and those fields are null in the look.

commits.description: Its commits from the line's base, its tip included.

foundBy.description: tipOnLine: a local branch whose tip is a commit of the line. named: named with --layer.

worktree.description: The worktree the branch is checked out in; null when it is in none.

state.description: What holds the layer's worktree: none (in no worktree), clean (nothing), dirty (tracked changes), rebasing (a rebase in progress, there or in another worktree that will move it), bisecting (a bisect in another worktree started from it), busy or idle (an agent session), process (a process whose working directory is inside the worktree), unknown (it could not be read, which holds the layer). In a run, as read when the layer was moved.

stateDetail.description: Who or what holds it: the session, the process, or why it could not be read.

newTip.description: The run's: the layer's new tip, read from the rebase and checked. Null in the look, and when the run moved no layer.

commitsAfter.description: The run's: commits of the new tip from the new base, as the check compared them with the plan.

mapped.description: The run's: tip (the new tip is its own tip rebased), tipDropped (trunk already carries its tip; the new tip is its last commit left), emptied (trunk carries every commit of it; it ends where the layer below does).

patch.description: The run's: whether what the layer brings to the line is the same patch as before, by git's stable patch-id. Never a refusal.

patchWhy.description: The run's: why the patch changed.

result.description: The run's: moved (the branch is at newTip, its worktree reset with it), held (left where it was; held says why and moveCommand moves it by hand), unchanged (its new tip is its old one), planned (recorded and not moved: the moves stopped before it), moving (its move was under way when the moves stopped: undo puts its ref back), needsRecovery (a move that went part way and could not be put back: held says what to look at, the layer keeps its pins, and wt sync undo puts it back).

how.description: The run's: ref (a branch in no worktree, moved with update-ref guarded by its old tip), worktree (reset --keep in its worktree, under that worktree's lock).

held.description: The run's: why the layer was held, or for needsRecovery what to look at.

moveCommand.description: The run's: what moves a held layer by hand.

pushCommand.description: The run's: for a moved layer, its push to its own remote as an argv, with a lease on the commit wt last fetched there. A run does not push layers. Null otherwise.

noPushReason.description: The run's: for a moved layer with no safe push command, why: no remote branch of its own yet, or the remote has commits the branch never had.

note.description: The run's: what else happened to a moved layer, such as a checkout of it that landed during its move, at its new tip.

stackSkipped.description: Since 1.7.0: a branch on the line not taken as a layer: a backup name (wt refs sweep's patterns), which --layer takes.
